name: PinchLens
summary: Bare-hand pinch selection for tiny, packed objects: starting a pinch opens a magnifying bubble around the fingertips and slows the virtual hand, and closing the pinch picks the target.
howItWorks: When the thumb and index tips come within 3.5 cm (semi-pinch) near a target, a spherical lens centred on the pinch point magnifies nearby targets in visual and motor space (sizes 4x, distances 3x, from a 1.67 cm area to a 5 cm sphere) and hides targets outside it. At the same time the virtual hand is slowed to half speed (adaptive control-display gain), a small cursor shows the pinch point, and a 1€-style filter steadies the hand. Completing the pinch selects the nearest target; afterwards the magnification ends and the virtual hand drifts back to the real one. In a pick-and-place study (N=12, Meta Quest 2 hand tracking, 0.75–1.5 mm targets, 500–1000 in an 8 cm cube 30 cm away), errors fell from 18.9% with plain pinching to 1.9%, with magnification as the main factor.

relationships.note: Inspired by the Bubble Cursor and Bubble Lens.
Adds magnification and slowed hand motion to direct pinch selection.
